question: Which medicine labels on MoleculeFinder list one of the six synthetic colour additives the FDA has asked food makers to stop using?

not_counted.reason: A separate registry record (a single chemical, CAS 860-22-0) that the registry lists as ONE COMPONENT of the FD&C Blue No. 2 record (L06K8R7DQK, a mixture of three components). It is not the same substance record as FD&C Blue No. 2, so it is not counted as Blue No. 2. One medicine label lists it (Keppra) and that label also lists FD&C Blue No. 2 by its own code, so counting it would move no total.

statements.title: Color Additive Petition From Center for Science in the Public Interest, et al.; Request To Revoke Color Additive Listing for Use of FD&C Red No. 3 in Food and Ingested Drugs (90 FR 4628)
statements.says: On January 16, 2025 the FDA published an order that removes the listings for FD&C Red No. 3 in food (21 CFR 74.303) and in ingested drugs (21 CFR 74.1303). The order takes effect January 15, 2027 for food and January 18, 2028 for ingested drugs.
statements.quote: This order is effective January 15, 2027, except for amendatory instruction 4, which is effective January 18, 2028.

statements.title: FDA to Revoke Authorization for the Use of Red No. 3 in Food and Ingested Drugs
statements.says: The FDA's own announcement of the order, dated January 15, 2025, gives the same two dates: manufacturers using FD&C Red No. 3 in food and in ingested drugs have until January 15, 2027 and January 18, 2028, respectively, to reformulate.
statements.quote: Manufacturers who use FD&C Red No. 3 in food and ingested drugs will have until January 15, 2027 or January 18, 2028, respectively, to reformulate their products.

statements.title: Micro-Tracers, Inc.; Response to Objections and Requests for a Public Hearing (91 FR 50475)
statements.says: A company's objections had put the order on hold from February 18, 2025. On August 5, 2026 the FDA denied the hearing request, lifted the hold and confirmed both dates, January 15, 2027 and January 18, 2028.
statements.quote: FDA lifts the administrative stay as of August 5, 2026. The effective dates of January 15, 2027, and January 18, 2028, for amendatory instruction 4, for the order published on January 16, 2025 (90 FR 4628), are confirmed.

statements.title: HHS, FDA to Phase Out Petroleum-Based Synthetic Dyes in Nation's Food Supply
statements.says: On April 22, 2025 the FDA and HHS said they would work with industry to eliminate six remaining synthetic dyes from the food supply by the end of 2026: FD&C Green No. 3, Red No. 40, Yellow No. 5, Yellow No. 6, Blue No. 1 and Blue No. 2. The announcement is about the food supply.
statements.quote: Working with industry to eliminate six remaining synthetic dyes—FD&C Green No. 3, FD&C Red No. 40, FD&C Yellow No. 5, FD&C Yellow No. 6, FD&C Blue No. 1, and FD&C Blue No. 2—from the food supply by the end of next year.

statements.title: Tracking Food Industry Pledges to Remove Petroleum Based Food Dyes
statements.publisher: FDA, page current as of October 16, 2026
statements.says: The FDA's tracker page, current as of October 16, 2026, describes the same six dyes as ones frequently used in the food supply and gives the end of 2027 as the date by which the FDA is working with food makers, retailers and trade associations to eliminate them. The page lists company pledges for food and does not mention medicines.
statements.quote: Additionally, the FDA is working closely with food manufacturers, retailers, and trade associations to eliminate six remaining certified color additives frequently used in the food supply—FD&C Green No. 3, FD&C Red No. 40, FD&C Yellow No. 5, FD&C Yellow No. 6, FD&C Blue No. 1, and FD&C Blue No. 2—by the end of 2027.

statements.title: Replacing Color Additives in Approved or Marketed Drug Products (draft guidance for industry, May 2025, docket FDA-2025-D-0507)
statements.publisher: FDA, Center for Drug Evaluation and Research
statements.says: In May 2025 the FDA published a draft guidance for drug makers on replacing a color additive in a medicine, whatever the reason for the change. It applies to prescription and over-the-counter medicines and sets out how a maker should test, document and report the change. It is a draft and not binding, and on November 21, 2026 the FDA still listed it as a draft. It names no dye to be replaced and gives no date.
statements.quote: This draft guidance provides recommendations for replacing color additives in approved or marketed drug products.

statements.title: Color Additives - Information for Consumers
statements.publisher: FDA, page current as of July 22, 2026
statements.says: The FDA regulates the color additives used in foods, drugs, cosmetics and certain medical devices. It describes a straight color as one not mixed or reacted with anything else (for example FD&C Blue No. 1) and a lake as a straight color reacted with precipitants and substrata (for example Blue 1 Lake).
statements.quote: The FDA is responsible for regulating all color additives used in foods, drugs, cosmetics (except for coal- tar hair dyes), and certain medical devices to ensure that they meet the FDA’s safety standard and are accurately labeled.

selection.chosen_by: A person picked them, brand by brand, in a list kept by hand (products.yaml). Candidates were drafted from the brand names the FDA's Drugs@FDA records give for medicines MoleculeFinder describes, and from brand names added by name (over-the-counter ones too), each with the brand owner's own label, not a repackager's.
selection.gate: A label needs at least three molecules MoleculeFinder holds, matched by the FDA's ingredient code, to have a page on the site.
selection.not_by: They were not chosen by sales, by how often they are prescribed or at random.
